Read all remaining non-exempt Markdown locations, including hidden directories.

Exempt evals directories at other positions and nesting depths.

obligations.statement: The lint rejects forbidden routing-table columns and a third table.

obligations.statement: The routing table carries the provider-tier model mappings and each model's price, context and accepted efforts.

parts.statement: Name the four outcomes in one defining passage and use them for the documented signal classifications and caller responses.
Do not make refusal imply that execution did or did not occur.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "choosing-a-delegate names the four outcomes any launcher reports"; "A refused invocation is one whose fix lies in the caller's invocation. That definition asserts nothing about what the run did or did not do."
obligations.statement: Choosing-a-delegate defines the four shared outcomes once, with refusal meaning that the fix lies in the invocation and without asserting whether execution occurred.

parts.statement: Teach the tested Codex read-only invocation and capture its stdout report in the caller's named file.
Classify the specified finished, background-running and usage-limit endings and collect the delayed report after the backgrounded process exits.
Identify the launched Codex process by pid when asked to stop it.
Supply correct permission distinctions and complete startup instructions for run kinds beyond the tested Codex read-only invocation and Google model-effort flag selections.
Supply Codex bounding guidance and agy bounding and stopping guidance.
Explain the OpenRouter clock flags and early stopping procedure.
Map every documented launcher signal to its shared outcome and document every script-emitted signal.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "Each launcher skill answers ... whether a run may write or only read; how each kind is started; which of its own signals means which outcome; how a run is bounded and stopped"; "delegating-to-codex gains its read-only run, with the output captured by the caller's shell, and the collection rule for a run that outlives the Bash call".
obligations.statement: Each launcher skill supplies its complete launch and supervision contract; the Codex skill includes caller-side read-only capture and collection after backgrounding.

parts.statement: End a wall-clock-expired run, including compliant and signal-ignoring children, in-group descendants and an open upstream response, with proxy closure and the specified failure report.
End the scripted idle cases, reset idle time on forwarded requests, and resolve the tested expiry and child-exit orderings.
End an idle-expired run whose last forwarded request still has an open upstream response.
Reject non-numeric, zero, negative and missing clock-flag values before proxy binding.
End the child when the launcher receives SIGTERM, including a signal-ignoring child.
Keep either or both clock flags and their values out of child argv and environment.
Accept positive fractional seconds as positive numeric clock-flag values.

obligations.source: DEL-D4: "run.js gains --timeout SECONDS and --idle-timeout SECONDS. On expiry it ends the child, closes the proxy, and exits 75 with a reason line on stderr"; "Idle means no completion request was forwarded for that many seconds"; "The flags are the launcher's own and never reach the child"; "A flag value that is not a positive number exits 78 before the proxy binds"; "A SIGTERM sent to the launcher ends the child even when the child ignores it".
obligations.statement: The OpenRouter launcher owns wall-clock and idle bounds, terminates the child and proxy on expiry, keeps the flags private, rejects invalid values before binding, and can stop a child that ignores SIGTERM.

parts.statement: Teach the two bounds, their expiry reports, early stopping, the low effort setting and the recorded durations.
Keep the Kimi whole-artifact constraint stated only once, in its owning launcher skill.

obligations.source: DEL-D4: "The OpenRouter skill states what each flag bounds and what expiry does, and records the measured durations of F9 as facts"; DEL-D2: "A constraint ... such as the Kimi K3 whole-artifact cap, lives in that launcher's skill, once"; section 6: "A whole-artifact read on moonshotai/kimi-k3 runs at low, stated once in the OpenRouter launcher skill."
obligations.statement: The OpenRouter skill explains its bounds and expiry behavior, records the measured durations, and owns the Kimi whole-artifact constraint once.

parts.statement: Choose and store the task-specific supervision settings at their stated ownership locations.

obligations.source: DEL-D4: "The dispatching skill chooses the values for its task and stores them alongside its effort and tool settings; the review panel's values live in its doctrine beside its seat pins."
obligations.statement: Dispatchers choose task-specific timeout values and store them alongside effort and tool settings; panel values live in its doctrine.

parts.statement: Teach the prescribed responses, including the allowed dead-run classifications and post-ingest gate.
Identify the Codex skill's read-only entry point and give no raw-codex-binary launch instruction under src.

A run the caller signalled means stop. Usable output is ingested with no claim, and the caller's own gate on an unread or unusable report still applies after ingest"; "Both callers name the Codex delegation skill's read-only run as the way a Codex reviewer is launched."
obligations.statement: The panel and ac-attack map shared outcomes to their own responses, preserve the post-ingest gate, and identify the Codex read-only entry point.

parts.statement: Respect the boundary in changed passages, eliminate run-lens terminology outside the two callers, and retain one shared definition.
Respect the signal and caller-vocabulary boundary in the remaining passages of those files.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "No launcher's signals appear in a caller's file. No caller's word, lens included, appears in a launcher's file."
obligations.statement: Caller files contain no launcher signals, launcher files contain no caller vocabulary, and shared outcome definitions have a single owner.

parts.statement: Keep text outside the DEL-D3 and DEL-D5 passages unchanged in every file slice C changes.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "Text outside the passages named here does not change."

obligations.source: DEL-D5: "The OpenRouter skill's description and body both require Edit(<path>) for a mandated report file."
obligations.statement: The OpenRouter skill's description and body both require Edit(<path>) for a mandated report.

Update contracts, lens front matter and emit_prompts.py to the provider representation.

Forward other admitted model-effort combinations and full variant identifiers unchanged.

Continue refusing Claude with or without the flag.

Mark all other ledger paths belonging to a run admitted by the flag.
Leave argv, environment, exit and ledger unchanged for models not refused.

parts.statement: Execute the isolated fixed-input scenarios three times, require every keyed answer, and count a missing answer as failure without retry.
Write scenarios, inputs and keys before their prose and commit them beside the evidence sidecar.

obligations.source: Section 5.4: "a fresh native subagent on the mid tier ... No other context is supplied. Each scenario runs three times"; "The scenarios, their captured inputs and their keys are written before the prose they test and are committed beside the evidence sidecar"; "A run that returns no answer is a failed run and is not retried."
obligations.statement: Scenario verification uses the prescribed isolated participants, fixed inputs, three-run threshold, no-answer failure rule and preregistered committed scenarios.

ground.reason: DEL-D3 promises run-bounding guidance, while DEL-D2 separately places model-specific constraints in the launcher skill. DEL-C2 combines clock operation, Kimi effort selection and recall of measured durations. These results can be delivered and judged independently, although its check groups scenarios C2a–C2e into one acceptance decision.

objections.objection: DEL-C2 makes acceptance of correct clock guidance depend on independently deliverable effort and duration guidance.

scenario.expect: The clock checks pass while the effort and duration outcomes remain absent; the bundled criterion cannot separately accept the delivered clock guidance.
scenario.given: The skill correctly explains both timeout flags, expiry results and early termination, but omits the Kimi effort and measured durations.
scenario.when: DEL-C2's keyed clock scenarios run.

ground.reason: DEL-D9 promises that 'The launcher holds no list of levels or models.' DEL-G2 repeats this obligation, but its named check observes fake-spawn arguments and refusal results for selected inputs, including zzz. Those observations cannot establish that the launcher contains no model or effort inventory.

objections.objection: A launcher can pass every specified refusal and forwarding case while retaining a second model or effort inventory.

scenario.expect: All specified checks pass while the promised absence of a launcher-owned inventory is unmet.
scenario.given: The launcher forwards every DEL-G2 fixture unchanged and translates the simulated refusals correctly, but also contains a model-and-effort inventory used for other selections.
scenario.when: DEL-G2's fake-spawn suite runs its specified cases.

ground.reason: DEL-V3 promises that 'a round in flight finishes on the version it started on.' Its check names suite coverage, including rejection of previous-schema records, and a run of the re-keyed scenarios. It names no check that an existing round can actually finish using its original version.

objections.objection: Correct rejection of previous-schema records can be accepted while an existing review round is stranded.

scenario.expect: The named checks pass while the unfinished round cannot complete on the version it started on.
scenario.given: The new tooling implements the provider fields and coded previous-schema refusals, but replaces the executable version needed by an unfinished old-schema round.
scenario.when: DEL-V3's suite checks the renamed interfaces and previous-schema refusals, and the re-keyed scenarios run.

ground.reason: The specified fixtures do not cover model identifiers in all the Markdown contexts the lint promises to read.

objections.objection: An unlisted model identifier can escape detection outside the tested sentence, fence and table forms.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the lint accepts the unlisted identifier in a Markdown link label.
scenario.given: The lint handles the prescribed fixtures but strips Markdown link labels before checking identifiers.
scenario.when: A scanned file contains an unlisted model identifier as a link label.

ground.reason: DEL-A6 exercises particular row forms; it does not establish detection across the remaining table layouts.

objections.objection: A second model inventory can use a table layout the lint does not recognise.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the additional table is accepted.
scenario.given: The lint recognises the prescribed table fixtures but checks identifiers only in their tested column positions.
scenario.when: Another Markdown table places a listed model identifier in a different column.

ground.reason: The checks sample file locations and report files read; they do not establish that every non-exempt Markdown file is read.

objections.objection: The lint can omit non-exempt files.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the hidden-directory file is never checked.
scenario.given: The lint traverses the tested directories but skips directories whose names begin with a dot.
scenario.when: An unlisted model identifier is added to src/.notes/guide.md.

ground.reason: DEL-A4 covers two directory arrangements, while the exemption applies to any evals directory under src.

objections.objection: The lint can reject an exempt evaluation file at another nesting depth.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the lint reads and rejects the exempt file.
scenario.given: The implementation exempts evals directories only at the depths exercised by DEL-A4.
scenario.when: A deeper evals directory contains a trigger query naming an unlisted model.

ground.reason: Restrictions on extra columns and tables do not establish that the required mappings and metadata are present.

objections.objection: The routing table can retain the permitted headings while losing required information.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the routing table lacks some promised tier mappings and per-model metadata.
scenario.given: The table keeps its model identifiers and the Google cheap-tier settings used by the scenarios, but omits another provider's tier mapping and leaves price or context cells empty.
scenario.when: The lint and scenario checks run.

ground.reason: The outcome questions test classification and caller responses, but not the explicit restriction on what a refusal implies about execution.

objections.objection: The shared definition can incorrectly guarantee that a refused invocation performed no work.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the definition adds an execution guarantee the decision expressly excludes.
scenario.given: The sole outcome-definition passage correctly says a refusal requires fixing the invocation, then also says that no work has run.
scenario.when: Readers answer the prescribed outcome and response questions.

ground.reason: The checks cover a Codex read-only invocation and selected Google model flags, but not the complete instructions distinguishing read-only and write-capable launches.

objections.objection: Launcher skills can give incorrect permission or launch instructions for untested run kinds.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but a worker following the documented grant cannot write, or a purported read-only launch permits writes.
scenario.given: The tested Codex read-only recipe is correct, and the tested Google commands carry the expected model and effort flags, but another launch recipe gives the wrong mode or tool grant.
scenario.when: A caller follows that untested recipe.

ground.reason: Naming the Codex process to stop does not establish bounding instructions, and the Google flag scenarios do not check supervision instructions.

objections.objection: The Codex or agy skill can fail to explain how its run is bounded and stopped.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the caller cannot obtain the promised bounding procedure from the skill.
scenario.given: The skills preserve the tested launch commands, classification answers and Codex stop-by-pid answer, but omit Codex bounding guidance or agy supervision guidance.
scenario.when: A caller holding only the relevant launcher skill needs to bound the run.

ground.reason: DEL-B1 tests an open upstream response for wall-clock expiry; DEL-B2 does not require that case for idle expiry.

objections.objection: An open upstream response can prevent the idle watchdog from ending a run.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but idle expiry leaves the child and proxy running.
scenario.given: Wall-clock expiry handles open responses correctly, while the idle-expiry path waits for an outstanding upstream response to close.
scenario.when: One completion request is forwarded, its response remains open, and no further request is forwarded for the idle interval.

ground.reason: Invalid-value checks and integer-duration examples do not require accepting positive fractional seconds.

ground.reason: The set requires a reader to map the OpenRouter launcher's `timeout` and `idle` signals onto exactly one of the four outcomes, but no criterion states which outcome a launcher-side timeout is. DEL-D4 deliberately reuses the agy exit contract, under which DEL-D3 assigns exit 75 to 'the provider did not serve the run', while DEL-D3's own dead-run description ('a run the caller's own watchdog killed for silence') describes the same circumstance as a killed run. The two readings demand different verdicts from the same run.

objections.objection: The criteria let one killed run be claimed either `transport-error` (fail over to another transport) or `unusable-output`/`dead-run` (re-brief ladder), with nothing in the set deciding between them.
objections.obligation: DEL-D3's shared-outcomes vocabulary and DEL-D4's clock contract

scenario.expect: Scenario C3's committed key either accepts provider-not-served (75, `transport-error`, fail over) or unusable-output/dead-run (re-brief); the criteria support both keys, so the panel's response to the same dead run diverges depending on which reading the key author took.
scenario.given: An OpenRouter lens run whose launcher is started with `--timeout` and whose child goes silent; the launcher kills the process group and exits 75 with `reason=timeout`.
scenario.when: A reader holding only `openrouter-claude-subagent` is asked, per DEL-C3, to name which of the four outcomes the `timeout` signal is, and the panel then maps the outcome to a claim reason.

ground.reason: DEL-G8 keys acceptance on agy's refusal message for `gemini-3.1-pro --effort medium` naming exactly `low, high`, but the only probe recorded (F17, on 2026-10-04) exercised `gemini-3.8-flash`; that gemini-3.1-pro lacks `medium` and words its refusal that way is asserted nowhere as verified.

objections.objection: If gemini-3.1-pro in fact accepts `medium`, or names its levels differently, a correctly implemented DEL-G1/G2 fails the criterion's key, and a wrong implementation could be tuned to pass it.

scenario.expect: The run exits 0 with the first line in its response instead of the keyed exit 78 with `low, high` on stderr, so the criterion fails although the launcher behaves as DEL-D9 requires.
scenario.given: agy 1.2.16 installed; `gemini-3.1-pro` actually lists `medium` among its levels (a possibility the spec never excluded).
scenario.when: The implementer performs the DEL-G8 run `agy_run.py lens --model gemini-3.1-pro --effort medium` over the one-commit repository and compares the result to the criterion's key.

ground.reason: DEL-B5 tries the flag values at the empty and low end — a flag given with no value, non-numeric, zero, negative — and DEL-D4 refuses only 'a flag value that is not a positive number', but no criterion tries the high end: a positive number of seconds larger than the launcher's process timer can represent is neither refused nor bounded, and what the launcher then does with it is stated nowhere.

objections.objection: The criteria let a well-formed --timeout or --idle-timeout value beyond the timer's representable range through the exit-78 check, where it can wrap to a near-immediate expiry or never fire, so the caller gets either a healthy run killed at launch or no bound at all.

scenario.expect: Per DEL-D4 the value is refused with exit 78 before the proxy binds, or the run is bounded by the value the caller chose; no criterion checks that an overflowing value yields one of these rather than a reason=timeout (or reason=idle) kill moments after launch, or a run left unbounded — F9's 67-minute run reborn, or its inverse, a healthy run ended at start.
scenario.given: An OpenRouter run started with --timeout (or --idle-timeout) set to a positive whole number of seconds beyond the range the launcher's timer can honour.
scenario.when: The launcher accepts the value, binds the proxy and arms the expiry.

ground.reason: DEL-V2 makes emit_prompts.py refuse an unknown provider value with a coded error, and DEL-D8 says the panel's data and code carry provider with exactly the four values; DEL-V3 checks the gate on those four values, on refusing --transport, and on refusing previous-schema ledgers and verdicts, but never on a fifth --provider value.

objections.objection: The criteria let dispatch_gate.py claim accept and record a provider outside the four values, and the bogus value flows on through the ledger, the verdict envelope, assemble_verdict's distinct-vendor count and prgroom's rendering.

scenario.expect: By DEL-D8's closed vocabulary and the standard DEL-V2 sets for emit_prompts.py, the gate refuses the value with a coded error naming the field and records nothing; unchecked, the unknown provider is recorded, counts as its own vendor in DEL-V5's total, and reaches prgroom's posting as a provider that does not exist.
scenario.given: A claim handed to dispatch_gate.py as claim --provider gemini — a plausible slip for the value google, and not one of anthropic, openai, google, openrouter.
scenario.when: The gate records the claim and the round's verdict envelope is assembled and posted.

ground.reason: DEL-V3 guarantees a round in flight finishes on the schema version it started on, so previous-schema verdicts exist while the rename lands, and it gives the panel's gate a coded refusal for them; DEL-V4 checks prgroom only with a fixture of the new version, and no criterion gives prgroom the same refusal, so its behaviour on a previous-schema verdict is unspecified.

objections.objection: The criteria let a previous-schema verdict — the very artifact the never-migrate rule says will be in flight — reach the updated prgroom, whose rendering of it is tested nowhere: it can post a verdict showing no provider for any lens, or fail without a coded error.

scenario.expect: By DEL-V3's never-migrate rule the verdict is refused with a coded error naming the field, as the panel's own gate refuses it, so the round's result is reported as stranded rather than silently mis-rendered; no criterion checks this, so the verdict can be posted and rendered with no provider named for any lens.
scenario.given: A review round in flight on the previous schema version when slice E's version bump lands, holding a finished verdict envelope whose fields are still transport and transport_error.
scenario.when: That verdict is posted through the updated prgroom post-verdict.
